method: After drafting and compiling, returned to actual current external Costs and Benefits of Criminal Policy, Forensic Psychology and Evidence, Cybercrime and Theoretical Criminology descriptions/objectives. Then re-read actual UCR Criminal Law and Criminal Justice, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Media and Race, Microeconomics and Behavior, Higher Order Functions, Modern Sociology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Networks and Operating Systems, and AI Ethics profiles/topics/methods. Challenged the finished scope, two concepts, 25 external components, partial relationships and 28 modal texts. Same AI as author; no different agent/model/human endorsement.
strongestObjection: A generic law/psychology/social-science palette could obscure the actual criminological organizing subject, including offender/victim explanation, specialized police/prosecution practice, forensic evidence, cybercrime, economic crime policy and an integrated criminological research sequence. Excluding later unknown study cannot erase gaps already inside the confirmed core.
adjudication: Give those gaps full weight. UCR Criminal Law and Criminal Justice includes criminological/organized-crime research design, legal responsibility and punishment; Youth Resilience to Extremism teaches radicalization, risks/protection and evidence-based prevention with an actual recipient-reviewed project; Media and Race directly examines crime, punishment, incarceration and extremist propaganda. These substantive anchors combine with sustained social theory, qualitative fieldwork, R-based multivariate methods, economic choice/efficiency and behavioral development. This is a defensible broader response to the confirmed core, not a specialist Dutch Criminology degree. The policy direction retains those anchors while changing institutional/legal and public-response priorities.
adverseTest: If new required third-year study strengthens general theory/research, the limited core claim remains. If it adds intensive Dutch procedure, detention, drugs/organized crime or specialist culmination, full-degree comparability could change; none is used to support the core claim. Elective capacity/eligibility does not provide assumed academic contents. Known victimology, spatial criminology, police/prosecution, cybercrime and witness-method gaps remain visible in the core itself.
alignmentChallenge: Fourteen partial relationships are academically specific and bounded. Cognitive attention/memory foundations are related to forensic cognitive limitations, without asserting witness/interrogation/evidence valuation teaching at UCR. Lifespan development is relevant to offender-development questions but not detained-person experience. Modern Sociology supplies actual explanatory theories, not a complete criminological-theory sequence. Microeconomics supplies actual choice/behavior/efficiency/externalities, not formal crime-policy CBA. Eleven components remain unpaired; broader methods are not counted twice.
alternativeChallenge: Policy changes four substantive courses (30 EC each way), replacing more individual development/cognition with international legal reasoning, comparative institutions, identity/inclusion empirical work and conflict policy. A full cyber research schedule passes formal feasibility but does not teach cyber-offender/victim, criminal-market/network, interpersonal abuse and sanction inquiry as its organizing subject. Actual Python, Wireshark, SQL/prediction and AI-forensic content were credited; no title/software/professional checklist is used. Stop at two.
